reason: Conversation 2 recognised the Hotpoint/Indesit fire-risk programme on the first turn, told the homeowner not to run it unattended and to check the model/serial with Whirlpool's safety checker before further use, then correctly held the stop-use line after learning there was no modification sticker and no recall letter, explaining why neither is reassuring. Conversation 1 missed the recall entirely in its first reply and only mentioned the checker as an afterthought in turn two, after instructing a supervised test run on a potentially unmodified affected model, which is exactly the unsupported 'safe once cleaned' direction the ground truth flags. Both gave sound filter/condenser cleaning advice and neither pushed parts, but 2's safety ordering and honesty about the open modification question are decisive.
